head: 87757fc
target: Session start repairs a clone whose local core.hooksPath names a missing directory — it unsets the config, then installs the pre-push hook — and the installer never writes into a directory that a live core.hooksPath names, such as husky's; it prints the line to add instead.
incidental: scripts/selftest: five checks pin the stale-pointer repair, the keep-husky-alone behavior, and install's refusal under a live core.hooksPath

questions.prompt: Before this fix, a clone of an opted-in repo had local core.hooksPath=.githooks, and a pull just deleted the tracked .githooks directory. What happens on the next push from that clone?

options.label: git falls back to .git/hooks, so the gate still runs
git refuses the push with an error about the missing hooks directory
no hooks run at all: the push succeeds, ungated and unremarked
every hook except pre-push still runs from .git/hooks

key_points: git looks up hooks through core.hooksPath and nowhere else: a missing directory means no hooks run, not a fallback to .git/hooks
the push just succeeds — no error, no gate, and nothing tells the author the clone is ungated

the installer resolves its hook path through the same config, so before the fix a session start would have written through the stale pointer and recreated the directory the repo had just deleted, instead of restoring the gate where git looks by default

questions.prompt: Which core.hooksPath settings does the new session-start repair unset? Pick all that apply.

options.label: a local one naming a directory that no longer exists
a local one naming husky's live .husky directory
a global one naming a directory that no longer exists
a local one naming a real directory that git does not track

key_points: the repair unsets only a local core.hooksPath whose named directory is missing: the pointer can only be stale, so clearing it loses nothing, and the hook is then installed where git looks by default
a pointer to a real directory is a live hook manager's; the config is kept and the gate prints the one line to add instead
the test is whether the named directory exists, not whether git tracks it
the repair only ever rewrites the clone's own local config; a user's global config is never touched by a session hook

questions.prompt: The fix also makes the installer refuse whenever core.hooksPath is set, printing 'add this line to its pre-push hook' rather than writing the gate's hook into the directory it names. What breaks if the installer keeps writing there — for the user's setup, and for the gate's own reliability?
key_points: the directory a live core.hooksPath names belongs to another hook manager: writing into it edits a setup the user owns, from a background session hook, without asking
the file would sit in a directory another tool may rewrite or reinstall over, so the gate could silently vanish again — the exact failure this fix repairs
refusing keeps the choice with the human, who wires the gate into that manager's pre-push: the gate integrates instead of injecting
the old code was inconsistent — it advised when a hook file already existed there but silently injected when none did; the new rule holds whether or not a file exists

questions.prompt: Four fresh clones of an opted-in repo each start a session once, and sync runs in each. In which clones does own-your-diff's pre-push hook end up written into .git/hooks/pre-push? Pick all that apply.

options.label: a clone with local core.hooksPath=.githooks, whose directory a pull just deleted
a clone with local core.hooksPath=.husky, a real husky directory
a clone with no core.hooksPath at all
a clone with a global core.hooksPath pointing at a real directory of shared hooks

key_points: the stale local pointer is unset first, so that clone is gated like any other
a clone with no core.hooksPath is the normal path: the marker is seen and the hook lands in .git/hooks
a live directory named by core.hooksPath — local or global — receives nothing: the config is kept and only the advice line is printed
the hook only ever lands where git's default hook resolution looks, or nowhere at all, and a global setting is never rewritten by the session hook
